It is becoming f*cking dangerous: The Claude Code tool found absolutely every shot that I considered permanently deleted from my iPhone. Data spanning 4 years of photos and videos was continuously stored in a disguised system cache. Every application with permissions to the file system had direct access to them

I synced my smartphone with a MacBook to create a backup. Then I ran the Claude Code vulnerability scan mentioned in my previous post. The scanner unexpectedly flagged a folder that I had not even asked it to check, a system directory named PhotoData/Thumbnails containing over 183,000 items. Pictures, video clips, screenshots, absolutely everything I had gotten rid of

Archives for 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024. Shots I deleted instantly after taking them. Photos for which I manually cleared the Recently Deleted section. Originals that I double checked and erased a second time just to be safe. All of it was still stored there

What exactly was found in that cache:

A random photo of a recipe from a cookbook from 2023

Screenshots of shopping lists and notes with daily chores

Failed takes and blurry landscape shots deleted right during a walk

A screenshot of a bus schedule from 2022 captured for just a few seconds

Photos of price tags and store labels deleted right at the checkout

A saved meme image from social media that I deleted back in 2024

A total of 173,521 files. Some of them in original resolution. Everything neatly sorted chronologically starting from 2021

When you delete media on an iPhone, iOS simply removes it from your gallery and trash. In reality, iOS keeps compressed copies in the Spotlight search index directory. That is precisely how fast keyphrase search works on your phone. Apple never clears this area, not after a month, not after a year. Claims of permanent deletion are simply untrue

I decided to check the list of software that has permission to access Files and Folders. It turned out there were 19 of them: weather utilities, QR code scanners, PDF readers, and even an old flashlight app installed in 2021. Any of these applications could freely read the data I considered destroyed all this time

I cut down the list of these applications from 19 to 5 in just a couple of clicks

The beauty of modern technology is that it allows us to recall what we have long forgotten

THIS IS AN ABSOLUTE GOLDMINE  

The team at Anthropic just revealed one of the most effective techniques for Claude Code

The core concept: run Sonnet, Haiku 5.5, and Opus 5.5 simultaneously, letting each model focus strictly on what it does best

You get higher quality output while dramatically reducing token consumption, since every specific job gets routed to the optimal model

To spin up Claude Code with this setup, simply execute:  

⁠claude --model sonnet --advisor opus⁠  

Here is how the workload is split:  

> Sonnet 5.5 handles the primary session, writes code, and applies bug fixes
> Haiku 5.5 scans the codebase in parallel: performing searches, running grep queries, exploring docs, and auditing diffs
> Opus 5.5 acts as an on-demand advisor for critical decisions and approves final code diffs
> You stop burning expensive Opus context on routine tasks that don't require high-level reasoning

Opus intervenes exclusively during three specific scenarios:  

> Right before locking in an execution plan
> Whenever the exact same error triggers twice in a row
> Prior to marking a task as complete

Sonnet builds. Haiku scans and explores. Opus reviews

JEV engineering applies the exact same principle one layer deeper: routine execution forks that don't need high-level reasoning (determining which file to inspect, which tool to trigger, or whether to retry or stop) are processed by JEV in sub-milliseconds, leaving big models to handle only complex decision splits

The full architectural tree:

Sonnet 5.5 manages the primary session and modifies code

Search maps out the repository structure via Haiku 5.5

Grep locates call references using Haiku 5.5

Docs fetches API specifications through Haiku 5.5

Opus 5.5 serves as an advisor, reading the complete conversation history whenever consulted

JEV routes lightning-fast micro-forks in milliseconds

Feed this tree structure alongside the prompt below into Claude Code

Reconfigure my Claude Code workspace based on this architecture:

1. Run the primary session utilizing Sonnet 5.5, with Opus 5.5 designated as the advisor
2. Set up three read-only Haiku 5.5 subagents: search (maps out the repo), grep (locates call sites), and docs (retrieves API documentation)
